Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the failing test asserts
  - The test constructs a PoissonDistributionImpl with a negative mean (-1).
  - It expects a NotStrictlyPositiveException to be thrown and will fail otherwise.

- How construction flows in the implementation
  - PoissonDistributionImpl(double) delegates to PoissonDistributionImpl(double, double, int).
  - In the main constructor PoissonDistributionImpl(double p, double epsilon, int maxIterations), the mean is validated with:
    - if (p <= 0) { throw MathRuntimeException.createIllegalArgumentException(...); }
    - Afterwards, it sets fields: mean = p; normal = new NormalDistributionImpl(p, sqrt(p)); and assigns epsilon and maxIterations.

- Why the test fails
  - When p is negative (e.g., -1), the code throws an IllegalArgumentException (created through MathRuntimeException.createIllegalArgumentException), not a NotStrictlyPositiveException.
  - The test explicitly catches NotStrictlyPositiveException and will call fail(...) if a different exception type is thrown or no exception is thrown.
  - Hence, the mismatch in exception type (IllegalArgumentException vs NotStrictlyPositiveException) causes the test to fail.

- Relation to the issue report
  - The report mentions a constructor that calls overridable methods in the constructor and stores a NormalDistribution reference passed in. That is a design concern (calling overridable methods in constructors and mutability of an injected dependency).
  - However, the immediate test failure here is specifically due to the wrong exception type being thrown on invalid (non-positive) mean, not due to those design issues.

Conclusion:
The failure is caused by PoissonDistributionImpl(double, double, int) throwing a generic IllegalArgumentException (via MathRuntimeException.createIllegalArgumentException) when the mean is non-positive, whereas the API and test expect a NotStrictlyPositiveException. Converting the validation to throw NotStrictlyPositiveException (and ensuring all constructor paths enforce this consistently) will satisfy the test.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
